correctness.rationale: The product comprises m clique fibers and one cross-fiber edge between (i,f(j)) and (j,f(i)) per index pair. If a dominating set omits a clique fiber i, each (i,h) needs an occupied j with f(j)=h; thus f restricted to occupied indices must be surjective, forbidding empty cliques when f is nonsurjective. For empty-image colors C (c colors), if t_h occupied fibers have f-value h, each color h needs ≥max(t_h,c) selected vertices, and this is achievable by distributing the c demanded second coordinates across those fibers. For h in C setting t_h=1 minimizes cost; all h not in C have t_h=a_h. Choosing the c largest a_h maximizes savings and proves min(m,c²+Σ_{j>c}max(a_j,c)) for 1≤c≤r, with the n² bound, lower/upper Sierpiński numbers min(m,n)/m and n=2 spectrum {2,3,4,m}. Direct exhaustive closed-neighborhood domination of 65 independent small sorted profiles agreed. This uses no asymptotic extrapolation.

value.rationale: The domination number of each map-dependent product, not merely extrema across maps, is a natural graph invariant. The exact sorted fiber-profile law yields a small optimization algorithm, sharp general bounds and an arbitrarily gapped attainable spectrum for fixed factors; this distinguishes genuine network structure from routine restatement of generic domination bounds.
